placements.why: The envelope's content is an organizational directive controlling what knowledge should exist — a governance concern about managing knowledge assets, naming a category nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers.
placements.title: From knowledge accumulation to directed erasure as organizational practice
placements.frame: What knowledge does the organization direct to be retained, erased, or removed, and what do those directives enact about control over what may be known?

placements.title: Commanding the removal of named knowledge
placements.frame: What specific knowledge does the organization command to be forgotten or removed, and what does the act of commanding erasure — without negotiation or argument — enact about authority over what may be known?
placements.why: Both segments are imperative directives commanding erasure of specific named knowledge artifacts (fleet, contracts, routes), performed as bare hierarchical commands in flat matter-of-fact register. This names a thematic subject — directed knowledge erasure — that future envelopes could feed with additional erasure directives, retention policies, or knowledge-management decisions. No existing leaf holds this theme.
